## TL;DR

Round 3 closes review pass 2 on provider parity and honest cancellation. Both Tailscale and Hetzner poll through `scheduleBrowserCaptureResultPoll`, share `runValidationContainerReaper`, and `validate.sh` can reap quiet completed running captures at startup. Failed remote kills record `browser capture cancellation failed` with per-container detail instead of claiming success. Tree at handoff: `b4cbf8803` on `feat/remote-browser-capture-runner-never-exit` (local WIP checkpoint may advance when RepoOS commits).

## Work and rationale

Hetzner previously blocked on a single `runRemote` for captures; the control plane now races the same result.json poll as Tailscale via an extracted helper, then downloads artifacts after force-collect. The periodic reaper is also shared so Hetzner’s warm VM gets the completed-capture and stale validation sweeps while excluding in-flight container names.

Cancellation must not lie: aborting the local SSH channel is not the same as removing the container. Both providers now append an infra-marked event whose message starts with `browser capture cancellation failed` and lists each failed kill (timeout or SSH error text). Success paths keep the prior “cancelled outstanding…” wording.

Native Tailscale hosts skip Docker collection polling by design (`runner === "native"`); that exception remains documented in `docs/remote-validation.md`.

## Approaches tried

Duplicated poll loops were collapsed into `scheduleBrowserCaptureResultPoll` rather than a larger race abstraction—Tailscale still layers hang watchdog and gate-linger racers that Hetzner does not need. Reaper logic was already centralized in round 3’s first pass as `runValidationContainerReaper`.

## Challenges and blockers

Fixture tests must reject spurious collection probes so cancel races do not complete as `ok: true`. Live runner verification on thinkpad/bee/mini is still human-owned; unit and command-level tests cover the commands and races.

## Key learnings

Hung captures are fixed at three layers: runner exit, Mac-side collect-on-result.json, and reaper/startup reap. Observability for failed cancels is as important as the kill itself—retries depend on knowing a stale container may still hold the slot.
